items.title: Manny Gabriel Interview, 1965-07-27
items.q: I played in the band too when he was kids with Red Alton. That's why they hired him to play through me.

ctx.x: You could spell him, Tramon, but he could play like the devil. Yeah, that's what I heard, he couldn't read much. He wasn't much of a reader, so Frank played the Tramon and the Louis Dumaine, the trumpet, and that's what I told you about, the Clampy Clampy, he played the saxophone, what his name was then? He played the John Robichaud. McCurdy. He played the, and we had, let's see what else is in that band, it's a long time, and now it's hard for me to tell who played Ketor in the band, because I, for piano, I…
You're a buddy of the peace band, huh?

items.title: Percy Gabriel Interview, 1987-07-10
items.q: See all of us played with Rene. Yeah. My brother-law August played with him, my brother Clarence played with him, my brother Manny played with him and I played with him.

ctx.x: I guess Joe was too fat for that.

Rene, you see Rene was right in our neighborhood. Rene lived on Corn Eyre between Johnson and Gallows I think it was. Did he drink? Yeah, he used to drink but then he on the end of it he had to quit drinking. Because I think when I was working with him he didn't drink anyone. See all of us played with Rene. Yeah. My brother-law August played with him, my brother Clarence played with him, my brother Manny played with him and I played with him.
Well how was he playing when you were with him?
